entries.title: Registrant drawer: open uploaded files, edit Country and its follow-up questions
entries.summary: In the **Registrants** drawer, an answer to a file question is a link that opens the file. **Edit** offers **Country** as a list, even when it was never answered, and shows a follow-up question only while the answer it depends on applies. In the attendee portal, a saved country shows in **Edit registration** instead of *Choose…*.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Registration → Registrants → a registrant → Edit

entries.use_case: Staff open a registrant's uploaded CV or document from the drawer, and fill a missing country without the form losing its follow-up questions.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer's registration form has file uploads or questions that depend on Country.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Registration.
internal.gotchas: Saving a follow-up that depends on Country needs the next web-api release (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5004).
internal.talk_track: Open uploads from the drawer and edit Country with its follow-ups.

entries.title: Search all events works for team members added to particular events
entries.summary: **Search all events** on **Registrants** used to refuse team members who were added to particular events rather than to the whole organization. They can now use it, and it searches only the events they are on (and leaves out the member list).

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Registration → Registrants → Search all events

entries.use_case: Desk and finance staff invited to one event find a registrant by name or email without an organization seat.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an event-only team member reports an error from Search all events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Registration with event-only team members.
internal.gotchas: Their event role still applies: without View registrations on an event, its rows stay out.
internal.talk_track: Search all events now works for everyone on the event team.

entries.title: One vocabulary: Scores tab, Screener, and upload slots that say submissions
entries.summary: A Review plan's scores view is now the **Scores** tab, so **Review** is no longer a tab inside Review. The pre-scoring agent card reads **Screener**. Upload slots on **Program Settings → Files** say submissions and participants. **Ask** also checks whether you mean review plans or attendee surveys when you just say "evaluations".

where.path: Program → Collect & Review → Review

entries.use_case: Teams read the same words in the product, in Ask and in the Help Center: review plans and reviewers for committee scoring, surveys for attendee feedback.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks where the Review tab went in a Review Plan 2.0.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every customer using Review plans, upload slots or Ask.
internal.staff_path: Program → Collect & Review → Review → a Review Plan 2.0 → Scores
internal.gotchas: Routes still contain /evaluation; attendee survey links take ?language=fr|de|es.
internal.talk_track: Same product, one name for each thing.

entries.title: Buying the membership dues prices the registration as a member
entries.summary: A non-member who buys the membership dues in the same order — with **Join and register** or by ticking the dues as an add-on, on any registration type — now registers as a member at the member price, and **Review** shows *Member (joining today)*. Orders your team places with the dues get the same price.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Registration → Settings → Member pricing → Join and register

entries.use_case: Associations that sell membership with registration get the member price charged whenever someone joins in the same checkout, so nobody pays the non-member rate plus dues.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer offers Join and register, or sells membership dues as a registration add-on.
internal.who_should_get_it: Associations running Registration with member pricing.
internal.gotchas: The Sites form's Review label ships with the org portal; the price needs the web-api release with lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5009.
internal.talk_track: Join in the same checkout and pay the member price, whichever type was picked.

enable.path: Get started → Early Access → Preview → Registration

entries.title: Only the printing station can mark a badge failed
entries.summary: In **Station mode**, **That one failed** now works only from the station that printed the badge; another phone on the same desk link gets a refusal. Close the browser's print dialog before clicking on the station page, or start Chrome with `--kiosk-printing` to skip it.

where.path: Onsite → Check-in & badges → desk link → Station mode

entries.use_case: Teams printing badges at several stations keep the queue honest: a badge is only marked failed by the station that tried to print it.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs print stations onsite.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events using Registration with Onsite print stations.
internal.gotchas: Needs the web-api release with lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5012 (it adds a column). While Chrome's print dialog is open the page ignores every click, which looks like a dead button.
internal.talk_track: Each station owns the badges it prints; the queue shows which ones failed.

enable.path: Ask your Customer Success Manager to enable Credit Claiming; then Field event → Settings → Continuing education credit

entries.title: A field event's claim site opens on email sign-in
entries.summary: The CE claim site of a field event now carries the field event's name (not "— Learning") and opens on **Email** sign-in, since guests have no badge numbers. Conference claim sites still open on **Badge number**. The desk **Comp** walk-up button now reads *no charge*.

where.path: Field event → Settings → Continuing education credit → Claim link

entries.use_case: Guests of a dinner or workshop sign in to claim CE credit with their email straight away, on a page named after the field event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer awards CE credit on field events.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with the Credit Claiming beta running field events.
internal.staff_path: Field event → Settings → Continuing education credit
internal.gotchas: The title and email default need the web-api release with lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5012; before it the page behaves as before.
internal.talk_track: Field-event guests claim credit with their email on a page with the event's name.

entries.title: Registrants full-name search; Send now keeps its last run
entries.summary: Search **Registrants** by a full name ("Stan Staff"). **Send now** on Emails & SMS keeps its **Last run** after a reload, says why an email was not sent and tries it again on the next run. Conditional answers that depend on **Country** now save. Speakers whose role is set to **Do not register** read *Not registered · role not registered*, and machine-drafted email translations keep the spaces around merge tags.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Registration → Registrants

entries.use_case: Staff find people the way they say their name, open uploaded files from the drawer, and can fill a conditional answer without it being lost.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer edits registrants by hand, uses conditional questions on Country, or relies on Know before you go.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Registration.
internal.gotchas: Machine-drafted email translations made before this release keep their missing spaces until edited.
internal.talk_track: Search by full name, open files from the drawer, and conditional answers now save.

entries.title: Badge batches print each type on its own design; preview a design with a real registrant
entries.summary: **Print a batch** now prints every badge on its registrant type's design (the default for types without one), so a Press registrant in a mixed batch gets the Press badge; choose **Design** to put everyone on one design. In the designer, **Preview with a registrant** shows a real person's name, organization and type on the canvas and in **PDF preview**, rules included.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Registration → Badges

entries.use_case: Per-type badge designs print correctly in one batch, and staff can check a design against a real person before printing.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer prints badges for several registrant types (Press, Speaker, Exhibitor) at once.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Registration badges.
internal.talk_track: Badge batches print each type on its own design; preview a design with a real registrant.

entries.title: Web check-in desk: clearer messages for codes it cannot match
entries.summary: The desk's search box now reads **Search by name or company, or scan a badge**. A scanned code the desk does not recognise says **That is not a check-in code**, and a real code that no registration at this event holds says **No one at this event has that code**.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Onsite → Check-in & badges → desk link

entries.use_case: Desk staff can tell a wrong kind of code from a person who is not registered.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs check-in with handheld scanners.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running onsite check-in.
internal.talk_track: The desk now says why a scanned code found no one.

entries.title: Booth sales and floor map fixes: Remove hall asks first, the Map tab shows every booth, Rebook says what it skipped
entries.summary: **Remove hall** asks before it removes a hall and its booths, and will not remove one while booth sales use a booth there. The Booth sales **Map** tab keeps search, hall tabs and the legend off the plan so **Fit** shows every booth, and follows the admin language. **Hold booths** in Rebook says how many were held and which booth numbers were skipped.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Expo Sales → Request access

where.path: Expo → Booth sales; Expo → Floor plan

entries.use_case: Fewer surprises when reshaping halls and selling booths.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reshapes halls after selling has started, or rebooks last year's exhibitors.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Expo booth sales.
internal.staff_path: Expo → Booth sales; Expo → Floor plan
internal.talk_track: Remove hall asks first, the Map tab shows every booth, Rebook says what it skipped.

entries.title: Credit Claiming: Audit times in the event's time zone, ledger says how a claim was backed, CSV import lists every bad row
entries.summary: The **Audit** tab shows each claim's session time in the event's time zone with the zone named (*Dec 10 · 10:00 AM – 11:00 AM PST*), whatever time zone your browser is in. In the **Claims ledger**, an attendee's claim reads as the attendance behind it — **Imported attendance**, **Session scan** or **Check-in**, with *Claimed by attendee* underneath — instead of *Self-reported*. **Import CSV** under Credits per session counts rows it could not match (or that have no amount) as errors and lists each by line and reason.

enable.path: Preview → Credit Claiming → Request access

where.path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming

entries.use_case: Accreditation staff read audit times as the attendee saw them and can trust the ledger and the CSV import result when reconciling credit.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer audits credit claims across time zones or bulk-imports credit per session.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Credit Claiming.
internal.staff_path: Program → After the event → Credit Claiming
internal.gotchas: A CSV row with no amount used to import as 0 credit; it is now an error.
internal.talk_track: Audit times in the event's zone, the ledger names the attendance, CSV import lists every bad row.

entries.title: Surveys speak about attendee ratings; Review translated in French, German and Spanish; Interest Form rounds drop event-only settings
entries.summary: The Surveys wizard now talks about what attendees rate: **Headline rating**, **What are attendees rating?** and **Share the results — no login needed**, in English, French, German and Spanish. The Review pages, tabs and reviewer workspace say Review and Reviewer in French (relecture), German (Begutachtung) and Spanish (revisión). Interest Form rounds no longer offer the returning speaker badge and agent summary switches, and their review site no longer shows a Submission files block. The legacy review monitor shows a Review plan's score as a percentage again (80%, not 400%), and the Awards **Pricing** step's payment settings links open Payment settings.

where.path: Program → Collect & Review → Surveys; Program → Collect & Review → Review

entries.use_case: Teams running attendee surveys and committee review in French, German or Spanish see one consistent vocabulary.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer runs Review or Surveys with the admin or the review site in French, German or Spanish.
internal.who_should_get_it: Everyone using Review or Surveys.
internal.staff_path: Program → Collect & Review → Surveys; Program → Collect & Review → Review
internal.gotchas: About 420 rarely seen Review strings are still English fallbacks in French, German and Spanish; the rest of the Surveys wizard is English only.
internal.talk_track: Surveys talk about attendee ratings; Review is translated; Interest Form rounds lose event-only switches.

entries.title: Exhibitor portal: due dates in the event's time zone, a company switcher, and Log out that signs out
entries.summary: Deadlines in the exhibitor portal show the date the organizer picked, wherever the exhibitor is (they showed a day late east of the event). A contact on several companies at the event picks one from **Company**, and **Log out** now signs out of the site. The attendee web map draws images at the opacity set in the designer, and the Exhibit & sponsor page confirms an application with its requested total instead of an empty order.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Expo Sales → Request access

where.path: Exhibitor portal (Site)

entries.use_case: Exhibitors see the right deadline dates, and agencies can manage each brand they exhibit for.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an exhibitor in another time zone asks about a deadline, or an agency manages several exhibitors.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using the Expo exhibitor portal.
internal.talk_track: Exhibitor portal: due dates in the event's time zone, a company switcher, and Log out that signs out.

entries.title: Contracts now accessible to event-only team members; Ready Room download log fixed
entries.summary: Event team members who belong to an event but not the full organization can now view and manage **Contracts** according to their event role's permissions (e.g. an **Admin User** role with contracts grants sees only that event's contracts; a **Read only** role without grants receives a 403). Previously, these users received a 403 on every Contracts route regardless of their role. Separately, clicking **Download** on the **Apps → Ready Room** page or the **Capture → Live Transcribe** card no longer returns a 400 error — the download is logged and appears in **Org History** under "Ready Room download".

where.path: CRM → Contracts (org); Event → Apps → Ready Room / Marketing → Capture

entries.use_case: Events that use dedicated per-event staff (who are not full org members) can now give those team members the correct level of Contracts access via their event role, rather than having them blocked entirely. AV and production staff who are event-only admins can also download the Ready Room desktop app from the event Apps page without hitting an error.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that event team members cannot access Contracts, or when setting up Contracts for an org that uses event-only staff.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Contracts add-on who has team members assigned at the event level rather than the org level.
internal.staff_path: Event → Event Team → [user] → Role permissions → Contracts
internal.gotchas: Impersonation cannot be used to test Contracts for event-only users because org routes run as the impersonating admin — QA must sign in directly as the event-only user. The Ready Room download fix also extends access to event-team members of the specific event, not just org members.
internal.talk_track: Event-only staff with the right role grants can now open and manage contracts scoped to their event. The Ready Room download button on the event Apps page works for event admins too.

draft.docs_gap: The contracts-permissions guide should note that event-only team members (those without an org-level seat) are admitted to Contracts routes and scoped to their event's contracts by their event role grants; it should also clarify that org-only actions (template writes, settings, DocuSign connection) still require an org membership row.

entries.title: Registration details: all pages validated on leave; speaker URL error now translated
entries.summary: When leaving the **Details** step of a registration form, every page is now checked in order — so a required question revealed on an earlier page (for example, a visa number uncovered by a travel answer) stops the registrant and shows the error on the correct page before they can proceed. Separately, the "invalid URL" error on a speaker question in a session submission form now appears in the portal's language (French, German, Spanish, etc.) instead of always showing in English.

where.path: Registration → (attendee-facing registration form) → Details step; Portals → (session submission form) → Speaker section

entries.use_case: Registrants with conditional required questions (such as a visa number revealed by a travel question) are now caught and guided back to the right page before checkout fails. Speakers filling a submission form in a non-English portal see URL validation errors in their own language.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports that registrants are hitting a 422 error at checkout despite filling out the form, or that non-English portals show English-only validation messages on speaker URL fields.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using registration forms with conditional (revealed) required questions, or running multilingual portals with speaker URL questions.
internal.staff_path: Registration → (event registration form with conditional questions) → Details step
internal.gotchas: Only the URL error message on speaker questions is translated in this fix; other speaker validation messages (required, max length) remain English-only for now.
internal.talk_track: Conditional required questions on earlier registration pages are now enforced when a registrant tries to leave Details, preventing silent 422 failures at checkout. Non-English portals also show speaker URL errors in the correct language.

draft.docs_gap: The registration forms guide should note that all Details pages — including those revealed by conditional answers — are validated before the registrant can advance past the Details step.

entries.title: Stay signed in when a token refresh can't reach the server
entries.summary: Admins and speakers are no longer signed out when a token refresh fails because of a dropped connection, a 5xx error, or a laptop waking before Wi-Fi reconnects. Only an explicit server refusal (a 4xx that is not a timeout or rate-limit) ends the session. When the server is temporarily unreachable, a **"Can't reach Sessionboard"** notice appears with a **Try Again** button; the app recovers automatically when the connection returns.

where.path: Any page — shown automatically when the server is unreachable

entries.use_case: Organizers and speakers who open a laptop after it has been asleep, or who briefly lose Wi-Fi, no longer have to sign back in and lose their place — the app waits for the connection to return and picks up where they left off.

cs_action.note: A prod-us customer reported admins being signed out repeatedly; close the loop with them through the original support ticket.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer reports being unexpectedly signed out, especially after waking a laptop or on an unstable network.
internal.who_should_get_it: All customers — this is a default-on bug fix.
internal.gotchas: A genuine 4xx server refusal (e.g. a revoked session) still signs the user out immediately. Only transient network failures are preserved. The 'Connection error' toast appears on API calls during an outage unless the caller suppresses it.
internal.talk_track: Users on spotty Wi-Fi or who close and reopen their laptops will no longer be kicked to the login screen — the app shows a 'Can't reach Sessionboard' notice and recovers on its own when the connection returns.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that a temporary network outage shows a "Can't reach Sessionboard" notice with a Try Again button rather than redirecting to the login page, and that the session is preserved until the server explicitly refuses it.

entries.title: Release-notes email subscription requires a company email address
entries.summary: In **Community → What's New**, the **Release notes by email** toggle card is disabled for accounts with a personal email address (Gmail, Outlook, etc.) and explains that release notes are sent to company addresses only. Attempting to enable the toggle from a personal address shows an error instead of a false success confirmation.

where.path: Community → What's New → Release notes by email

entries.use_case: Organizers with a personal inbox no longer see a misleading success message when trying to subscribe to release-note emails; the card clearly explains that a company email address is required, so they know to sign in with their work account instead.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why they cannot subscribe to release-note emails or why the toggle is greyed out.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any organizer using Community / What's New.
internal.staff_path: Community → What's New → Release notes by email
internal.gotchas: Users on competitor domains (Cvent, Swoogo, etc.) do not see the card at all — this is intentional and enforced by the API.
internal.talk_track: The toggle is disabled for personal mailboxes (Gmail, Outlook, etc.); the user needs to sign in with their company email to subscribe.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the release-notes email toggle is disabled for personal email addresses and explain that a company address is required to subscribe.
draft.why_use_it: Release notes by email deliver a digest of new features and improvements directly to your inbox so your team stays current without checking the product manually. Subscribing takes one click from the What's New tab in Community, and emails go only to verified company addresses to keep delivery reliable.

entries.title: Ask runs reports in the same turn and hands off to support at once
entries.summary: Ask for a report and it runs it and shows the result, instead of asking "Shall I run it?" first; it no longer shows query syntax. **Contact support** hands you to the team straight away when Ask already knows the problem, and it gives the support email when you ask for it. It describes only what a tool confirmed was saved. Conversations are kept per event, so switching to another event no longer loses the request you left open, and approval cards stay put when you ask something else while one is waiting. Speaker Coordinator reply drafts use your event's pinned answers.

where.path: Ask (top bar)

entries.use_case: Organizers get answers and report results in one turn, and reach a person without repeating themselves when Ask cannot help.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer says Ask keeps asking before it runs a report, forgot what they asked after switching events, or would not give a support contact.
internal.who_should_get_it: Every organizer using Ask.
internal.gotchas: Reports were always read-only; only the extra confirmation turn is gone. Ask still does not volunteer the support email ahead of the Contact support hand-off.

entries.title: Import registrants starts with confirmation emails on every time
entries.summary: The **Send each new registrant their confirmation** box in **Registrants → Import CSV** is ticked again each time the dialog opens, like **Send the confirmation email** in **Add registration**. Unticking it once no longer leaves later imports without confirmations.

where.path: Registration → Registrants → Import CSV

entries.use_case: Teams that import comps or registrations in batches can be sure every new registrant gets their confirmation unless they untick it for that import.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports registrants from a later import never got a confirmation.
internal.who_should_get_it: Registration customers who import registrants or comps.
internal.gotchas: Registrants imported while the box was off still have no confirmation; use Resend confirmation on them.

entries.title: Attend Overview: engaged attendees, Attendee Health and Sponsor Health
entries.summary: **Attend → Overview** opens with **Registered → Active → Engaged** and two gauges: **Attendee Health** (engaged ÷ active) and **Sponsor Health** (the share of sponsors and exhibitors with at least one attendee interaction). **See who has none** lists the ones nobody has interacted with yet.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Overview

entries.use_case: Organizers see in one glance how many attendees really use the app and which sponsors are getting no attention, while there is still time to help them.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how engaged their attendees were, or how to prove value to sponsors during the show.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running the Attend app with sponsors or exhibitors.
internal.gotchas: Shown to Sessionboard staff first (super-user gate) and only once the next web-api release is live (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5022).
internal.talk_track: Registered, active, engaged — and which sponsors nobody has touched yet.

entries.title: Lead retrieval: see what a lead did at the event, with their consent
entries.summary: On a lead in the app, **At this event** shows the sessions the attendee checked into (the team's own tagged **Your session**), whether they saved the company or its products, page views and meetings with the team. Attendees choose on **My badge** (**Exhibitors who scan me can see the sessions I attended**); organizers set the default under **Lead retrieval → Settings**. The export adds the same columns.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Lead retrieval → Settings; the app → a team's leads → a lead

entries.use_case: Booth staff follow up with context — the sessions a lead sat in and the products they saved — without the organizer ever sharing data the attendee didn't agree to.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an exhibitor asks for richer leads than a name and a company.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers selling lead retrieval seats to exhibitors.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Lead retrieval → Settings; the app → a team's leads → a lead
internal.gotchas: Shown to Sessionboard staff first (super-user gate) and only once the next web-api release is live (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5022). The app part arrives with the next app update (lennd/sessionboard-mobile#125).
internal.talk_track: Leads that say what the person cared about at the show, with the attendee's consent.

entries.title: Lead retrieval: a Live view of scans per booth
entries.summary: **Attend → Lead retrieval → Live** shows leads per booth in the last hour, today and in total, active scanners and last scan, refreshed every 30 seconds. **Quiet booths only** shows teams with no scan in the last hour.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Lead retrieval → Live

entries.use_case: Floor staff see which booths are busy and which are dead during the show, and walk over to help the quiet ones.

internal.when_to_bring_up: During a show with lead retrieval, or when a customer sells booth traffic to exhibitors.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers selling lead retrieval seats to exhibitors.
internal.gotchas: Shown to Sessionboard staff first (super-user gate) and only once the next web-api release is live (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5022).
internal.talk_track: Every booth's scans, live — and a filter for the quiet ones.

entries.title: Attend app: points, quests, booth QR codes and a leaderboard
entries.summary: Attendees earn points in the Attend app for checking in to sessions, visiting booths, voting in polls and more, chase quests (including quests a sponsor pays for) and see their rank. Organizers set the points, quests and leaderboard on **Attend → Engagement → Gamification**, print a QR poster per booth, watch the live leaderboard, void an award and export the prize list. Off until turned on per event.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App, then ask your Sessionboard contact to turn on Gamification

where.path: Attend → Engagement → Gamification

entries.use_case: Sell a sponsored quest that sends attendees to the sponsor's booth, and show the sponsor the booth scans and completions it drove.

cs_action.note: The Gamification tab is staff-only while it rolls out: a Sessionboard super user turns it on for the event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers with exhibitors or sponsors who want booth traffic, or who ask about Highbar / Attendify-style points and leaderboards.
internal.who_should_get_it: Attend customers with sponsors or an expo floor.
internal.gotchas: Needs the next web-api release (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5024); the app and admin tab stay hidden until then. Leaderboard names only attendees listed in the attendee directory. The attendee screens ship in the Attend app (lennd/sessionboard-mobile#127), which reaches attendees on the app's own release, not on these deploys.
internal.talk_track: Points for what attendees already do, quests a sponsor can buy, and the booth numbers to prove it.

entries.title: Webinars: connect Zoom or Goldcast and import every webinar
entries.summary: Connect Zoom or Goldcast once from **Program → Webinars**, then bring in upcoming and past webinars with **Import from Zoom / Goldcast**. Past webinars arrive with registrants, attendance, engagement and the recording, and a connection whose sign-in expired shows **Sign-in expired** with a **Reconnect** button.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars

entries.use_case: Bring the webinars a team already runs in Zoom or Goldcast into Sessionboard in a few clicks, history included, so every registrant and attendee lands on the same contact record as the rest of their activity.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: Customers who run a webinar program on Zoom or Goldcast alongside their conference.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with a regular webinar series and an Enterprise or Marketing plan.
internal.gotchas: The Zoom app is still a Draft in the Zoom Marketplace, so only Zoom users on Sessionboard's own Zoom account can authorize it today; customers connect Goldcast (API key) or wait for the Zoom app review. Webinars sit under the Field Events Early Access (gatherings). Zoom past webinars come from the last 180 days.
internal.talk_track: Your webinars, history and all, in the same place as your conference.

entries.title: Webinars: draft here, publish to Zoom or Goldcast, keep it in sync
entries.summary: Create a webinar in Sessionboard and click **Publish** to create it in Zoom or Goldcast in five steps: the webinar, speakers as panelists, registration on your own page, join links in your confirmation email and Advocacy cards. **Sync now** pulls the latest on demand, and title, start time or duration changes made in the provider show up for you to keep or put back.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → Overview

entries.use_case: One place to edit the webinar, with your own registration page and confirmation email, while the provider still runs the room.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer copies webinar details between Zoom and their registration tool by hand, or gets surprised by hosts moving times in Zoom.
internal.who_should_get_it: Webinar teams who want registration and branding in Sessionboard.
internal.gotchas: The Zoom app is still a Draft in the Zoom Marketplace, so only Zoom users on Sessionboard's own Zoom account can authorize it today; customers connect Goldcast (API key) or wait for the Zoom app review. Webinars sit under the Field Events Early Access (gatherings). Goldcast takes registrants through the event's registration form; in testing Goldcast's documented registration call answered success without creating the registrant, so check a Goldcast registrant arrives before promising it.
internal.talk_track: Edit once here; the provider follows, and you decide when they disagree.

entries.title: Webinars: speakers, content and sponsors recommended for a topic
entries.summary: Write a webinar topic and click **Get recommendations**, or open **Program → Recommendations** on a webinar: Sessionboard lists the speakers who spoke on it across your events, related sessions, recordings and clips, and sponsors and exhibitors to approach, each with the evidence, plus a suggested draft.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: New webinar → Topic, and a webinar's Program → Recommendations

entries.use_case: Find the right speakers and sponsors for a webinar from the organization's own event history, instead of starting from a blank page.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer struggles to fill webinar speaker slots or sell webinar sponsorships.
internal.who_should_get_it: Organizations with several years of events in Sessionboard.
internal.gotchas: Recommendations read the whole organization's contacts; a role without Contacts access sees a request to ask an org admin.
internal.talk_track: Your past events already know who should be on this webinar.

entries.title: Webinars: a Plan board of webinar ideas by format and funnel stage
entries.summary: The **Plan** tab on **Program → Webinars** suggests webinars to run next, each with a format, a funnel stage, goal, metric and call to action, why now, and speakers from your contacts. Filter by stage and format, add a focus, and click **Draft this webinar** to start one. Three ideas also show at the top of the Webinars page.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → Plan

entries.use_case: Turn what the audience is asking about into a balanced webinar calendar, with speakers already picked from the organization's contacts.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer plans a webinar series or quarter and asks what to run.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing and education teams running a recurring webinar program.
internal.gotchas: Ideas are not saved: every visit draws a fresh board. Interest counts come from surveys and webinar engagement, so a new org with no history gets template ideas from its taxonomy and frequent speakers.
internal.talk_track: Ideas grounded in your own audience and speakers, a click away from a draft.

entries.title: Webinars: pre-webinar survey and attendance per registrant
entries.summary: On a webinar's **People** tab, **Create survey** writes a short pre-webinar survey from the topic and **Send to registrants** emails each person their own link. Their interests, goals and question show per registrant, and **Attendance & engagement** shows who attended, for how long and who did not show up.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → People

entries.use_case: Know what each registrant wants before the webinar and who actually came after it, so the host and the follow-up speak to them.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks how to learn more about webinar registrants or personalize follow-up.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any webinar customer.
internal.gotchas: The survey is a Pathways pre-event quiz but works without the Pathways Early Access. Attendance arrives with the first sync after the end time.
internal.talk_track: Ask them what they want, then see who showed up.

entries.title: Webinars: poll answers, questions and more per attendee, matched to the moment
entries.summary: After a webinar, Sessionboard reads the provider's reports and records each attendee's poll answers and questions (Zoom) or CTA clicks, ratings and feedback (Goldcast), with a timeline of the webinar and the chapter that was playing. Each one is tagged with your topics and feeds Pathways.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → People → Attendance & engagement

entries.use_case: See who engaged with which part of a webinar, and let that interest flow into Pathways, session picks and HubSpot.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants to know which webinar attendees are warm, or asks for webinar data in their CRM.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers on Pathways or with HubSpot connected.
internal.gotchas: Zoom reports polls and Q&A only; neither provider exposes chat or reactions through its API. Moments fill in once the recording is chaptered.
internal.talk_track: Not just who came, but what they cared about.

entries.title: Webinars: recording into Media with chapters, clips and a social pack
entries.summary: When the webinar ends, its cloud recording comes into **Media**, is transcribed from its audio and chaptered, and the best moments are suggested as clips. The **After** tab shows the clips with copy per network and a **Social pack** of LinkedIn, X, Instagram and newsletter posts.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → After

entries.use_case: The week after a webinar, the clips and posts are already written, so the recording gets promoted while it still matters.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says their webinar recordings sit unused.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers with Media and a recurring webinar program.
internal.gotchas: Suggested clips must be cut in Media to get a video file. A Goldcast recording carries no length, so the Media item's duration comes from the webinar until the file is processed.
internal.talk_track: The recording turns into a week of posts on its own.

entries.title: Webinars: a personal recap for every attendee and no-show
entries.summary: **Personalised follow-up** on a webinar's **After** tab builds one recap per person: the clips closest to their interests and the moment they asked a question, answers to their questions, and the recording for no-shows. Preview any recap, send in batches of 200, or export a CSV for your marketing tool.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → After → Personalised follow-up

entries.use_case: Replace the generic thank-you email with a recap each attendee actually opens, built from what they told you and what they did.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks for better webinar follow-up or on-demand views.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any webinar customer with recordings.
internal.gotchas: Recaps need the recording and clips, and attendance from the provider; the headline and intro are templated, not AI-written.
internal.talk_track: Every attendee gets the part of the webinar they came for.

entries.title: Dispatch: send webinar clips to your team, who post from their own share kit
entries.summary: **Share with your team** on a webinar's **After** tab creates a Dispatch with the clips and posts, by **Slack**, **Email** or both. Each teammate opens their own share kit: your **Why we're sharing this**, a day-by-day schedule, copy to make their own and **Post to LinkedIn** with their tracked link, with progress for them and the team.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → After → Share with your team

entries.use_case: Get the whole team posting the webinar clips on schedule, and see who did, without chasing anyone in Slack.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants employees or members of staff to promote their webinars.
internal.who_should_get_it: Marketing teams with sales or member-facing colleagues on LinkedIn.
internal.gotchas: A webinar Dispatch works for anyone who can open the webinar; other Dispatches still need the Dispatch Early Access. LinkedIn posting needs each teammate to connect LinkedIn once in the kit.
internal.talk_track: Your team posts the clips, and you see who did.

entries.title: Dispatch: every teammate gets a Slack message and an email with one button to their share kit
entries.summary: Sending a Dispatch now reaches each person by Slack direct message and by email, and both carry one button, **Open your share kit**, instead of a link or file. Slack channels are told to look for the direct message, and nudges remind only the people who have not posted yet.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Marketing → Dispatch, and a webinar's After tab

entries.use_case: Posting happens from the share kit, so every share is tracked and counted, and a missed Slack message still leaves the ask in the inbox.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer asks why Dispatch shares are not being counted, or wants reminders for teammates who have not posted.
internal.who_should_get_it: Dispatch customers.
internal.gotchas: Slack link buttons show Slack's 'not configured to handle interactive responses' warning until the Interactivity Request URL is set on the Slack app (lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5016, staff config).
internal.talk_track: One button, one place to post, every share counted.

entries.title: Webinars: Advocacy for speakers, co-presenters and attendees on publish
entries.summary: Publishing a webinar turns on Advocacy for it: every confirmation email carries the registrant's share card, and each speaker and co-presenter gets their own tracked share link, listed on the **After** tab with **Copy link**. Co-presenters added in Zoom, Goldcast or under **Program** get a link on the next sync.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Program → Webinars → a webinar → After → Advocacy

entries.use_case: Every webinar gets promoted by its speakers and registrants from the day it is published, with each person's shares counted.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer wants more webinar registrations without more ad spend.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any webinar customer.
internal.gotchas: Sessionboard does not email speakers their link for webinars (the provider sends panelist links); the organizer passes it on. Needs the Advocacy create/update permission on the webinar.
internal.talk_track: Speakers and registrants promote every webinar, tracked.

entries.title: Generated social copy reads like a person wrote it
entries.summary: Every post Sessionboard writes for you, in a webinar's social pack, in Dispatch and in Advocacy share copy, now follows the same rules: no em or en dashes, no emoji, none of the stock AI phrases, and hashtags last on one line. Copy you type is never changed.

enable.path: Organization → Preview → Field Events → Request access

where.path: Webinar social packs, Dispatch posts and Advocacy share copy

entries.use_case: Posts that teammates and speakers are happy to publish under their own name, without editing out the tells of AI copy first.

cs_action.note: Webinars ride on the Field Events Early Access: turn it on for the org, then help them connect Goldcast, or Zoom once the Zoom app is approved.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer says generated posts sound robotic or full of emoji.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers using Advocacy, Dispatch or webinar social packs.
internal.gotchas: Applies to newly generated copy; posts generated before this release keep their wording until rewritten.
internal.talk_track: Generated posts that sound like your team.

entries.title: Attend app: a Now block on Home with a live AI summary and Ask chips
entries.summary: A **Now** block at the top of the app's Home summarizes what's on now and in the next 90 minutes, greets the attendee by first name, and offers an **Ask anything** box and question chips that open Ask. **Auto** writes it from the program; **Organizer prompt** adds your guidance.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Publish → Mobile App → Home → Now card; the app's Home

entries.use_case: Attendees open the app and see in plain words what's happening right now, with one tap to ask about it.

cs_action.note: Staff-only during rollout (super user): staff set it up for the event on request.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an organizer wants Home to feel live during the event, or asks for an AI summary like Highbar's.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend app Early Access beta with Ask on.
internal.staff_path: Publish → Mobile App → Home page → Now card (staff only for now)
internal.gotchas: Off by default per event. The summary counts toward Ask's daily AI budget and needs org AI features on; chips need Ask on. Needs the web-api release with #5025 and the app update with #126. The attendee side ships in the Attend app (lennd/sessionboard-mobile#126, EAS update; production is a manual promotion).
internal.talk_track: Turn on Now and your app's Home tells attendees what's on now, every few minutes.

entries.title: Attend → Ask: see what attendees ask and pin an answer
entries.summary: A **Topics** tab on Attend → Ask groups attendee questions into topics with counts only (attendees asking, share answered, 👎, sent to your team). **Pin an answer** on a topic and Ask gives it to anyone who asks about that topic, however they word it.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Ask → Topics

entries.use_case: Organizers see the questions their program doesn't answer and fix them in one step, without ever reading attendees' questions.

cs_action.note: Staff-only during rollout (super user): staff set it up for the event on request.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an event's Ask shows a high 'Answered without a source' share, or during a live event to tune Ask.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend app Early Access beta with Ask on.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Ask → Topics (staff only for now)
internal.gotchas: Topics appear only once 3+ attendees ask about the same thing, and are built nightly; a new event shows the empty state. Needs the web-api release with #5025.
internal.talk_track: See what attendees keep asking and pin the answer.

entries.title: Ask answers event facts like the Wi-Fi password, with a Copy button
entries.summary: Add **Event facts** on Attend → Ask — Wi-Fi, parking, badge pickup, dress code — and Ask quotes them word for word as a card in the app, with a **Copy** button for codes. Facts stay attendee-only unless you mark them for the public website.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Ask → Event facts; the app's Ask answers

entries.use_case: The logistics questions that swamp the help desk get exact, copyable answers in the app.

cs_action.note: Staff-only during rollout (super user): staff set it up for the event on request.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an organizer mentions repeated Wi-Fi, parking or badge-pickup questions, or before any event goes live with Ask.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend app Early Access beta with Ask on.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Ask → Event facts (staff only for now)
internal.gotchas: Copy opens the phone's share sheet (which has Copy) in the current app build. Needs the web-api release with #5025. The attendee side ships in the Attend app (lennd/sessionboard-mobile#126, EAS update; production is a manual promotion).
internal.talk_track: Put your Wi-Fi password in Event facts and Ask hands it out with a Copy button.

entries.title: Sell an Ask header sponsor credit, and give attendees a way out when Ask can't answer
entries.summary: A new **Ask header** sponsor placement shows a short line with the partner's logo at the top of Ask, counted in Analytics with the other placements. When Ask declines or can't cite a source, the app offers your **Support email** under the answer.

enable.path: Event → Admin Settings → Early Access → Attend Mobile App

where.path: Attend → Sponsor ads → New placement → Ask header; Attend → Ask → Support email; the app's Ask screen

entries.use_case: Organizers add a new sponsor line item to sell, and attendees who hit a question Ask can't answer reach a person instead of a dead end.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer sells app sponsorships, or asks what happens when Ask doesn't know.
internal.who_should_get_it: Events on the Attend app Early Access beta with Ask on.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Sponsor ads → New placement; Attend → Ask → Support email (staff only for now)
internal.gotchas: The Ask header slot shows in the placement editor only once the web-api release with #5025 is live. Support email is staff-only for now. The attendee side ships in the Attend app (lennd/sessionboard-mobile#126, EAS update; production is a manual promotion).
internal.talk_track: Sell the Ask header to a sponsor; set a support email so no attendee is stuck.

entries.title: Cancelling an order paid with a credit gives the credit back
entries.summary: When a registrant cancels an order they paid with a credit, or you **Cancel under the policy**, the refund for that part now comes back as a new credit for the same amount (no bonus) instead of a check you owe. Card payments still go back to the card, and only check, PO or wire payments are added to **Refunds to issue**. The attendee portal, the cancellation email and the order's **Payments** say where the money went.

enable.path: Event → Preview → Registration → Request access

where.path: Registration → Orders → an order → Cancel under the policy…

entries.use_case: A registrant who paid with last year's credit cancels and gets the credit back instead of waiting for a check.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a customer issues credits for cancellations or event moves.
internal.who_should_get_it: Customers running Registration with a cancellation policy.
internal.gotchas: Staff who pick a refund method (check, wire) still get that method; 'Give a credit instead' still adds the policy bonus.
internal.talk_track: Money paid with a credit goes back to a credit, automatically.

entries.title: Session recaps from an uploaded recording, published to the Attend app
entries.summary: Upload a recording on a session's **Recap** tab in **Attend → Engagement** and get a recap in a few minutes: summary, takeaways, chapters, quotes, stats cited, people and companies, and the transcript. Edit or hide any section, then publish it to a **Recap** tab in the app with **Ask about this talk**. **Off the record** keeps a session from taking a recording.

enable.path: Sessionboard staff only for now (not yet released to customers)

where.path: Attend → Engagement → Sessions → a session → Recap

entries.use_case: Sessions that weren't captioned live still get a recap: the organizer drops in a phone recording after the talk, checks the draft and publishes it to the app, where attendees can read it and ask questions about it.

cs_action.note: Staff-only for now: the Recap tab shows to Sessionboard staff until it is promoted.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer has sessions without Live Transcribe, or wants post-event content from recordings.
internal.who_should_get_it: Not customers yet: the Recap tab shows only to Sessionboard staff until it is promoted. Then: Attend app events that record sessions but don't caption them live.
internal.staff_path: Attend → Engagement → Sessions → a session → Recap
internal.gotchas: Needs the web-api release with lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5042; until then the tab does not appear. Transcription is audio-only. Quotes and stats not found in the transcript are dropped. The app's Recap tab ships in the Attend app (lennd/sessionboard-mobile#131, EAS update), which the release job does not track.
internal.talk_track: Drop in the recording, edit the draft, publish: the app gets a recap and Ask can answer questions about the talk.
